description.narrative: The widespread use of explosive weapons in the ongoing conflict has been adding extensive layers of explosive ordnance contamination across the country, including major cities and other urban centers as well as critical infrastructure like roads, schools, hospitals, and airstrips. These hazards pose a direct threat to life and limb of those living in these areas as well as those displaced considering returning. They also pose a barrier to safe delivery of humanitarian aid and block safe access for civilians. The only way to remove these threats is to conduct large-scale surveys and clearance operations through trained mine action teams. Specialized equipment is required to conduct these operations safely and comprehensively in line with international and national mine action standards. Since all of the prior mine action equipment was looted or lost during the conflict, the mine action sector is unable to respond to the now massive and increasing survey and clearance needs. As bringing new mine action equipment into Sudan is time-consuming and can create a bottleneck in the planned scale-up of survey and clearance operations, this project proposes to procure technical equipment needed so that survey and clearance activities can begin without delay. The procured equipment will be available to mine action operators who meet the international mine action standards to operate in Sudan.\n\nEstablished in 1997, the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) leads, coordinates, and implements projects and programmes to mitigate the threats posed by explosive ordnance to the benefit of millions of people worldwide. UNOPS works with UNMAS to address the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance.
